title: One of Hampstead's oldest pubs has been named among the most haunted in the UK
excerpt: Hampstead’s historic The Spaniards Inn ranks fifth among the UK’s most haunted pubs, with ghostly tales of Dick Turpin, a spectral horse and three resident spirits.
content:
One of Hampstead's oldest pubs has been named among the most haunted in the country.

The Spaniards Inn, which dates back to 1585, claimed fifth place in a national ranking with at least three resident ghosts and a spectral horse heard on the road outside.

The ranking of the spookiest watering holes was compiled by card machine provider Dojo, based on Reddit threads, online reviews, and reports from pub landlords.

But Hampstead residents have long known that the Spaniard's, with its low beamed ceilings, open fires and dark wood-panelling has a special atmosphere.

The pub has a long history of eerie sightings and chilling tales which perhaps inspired Dracula author Bram Stoker to put it in his book.

Charles Dickens was also a former patron - he lived for a summer not far away in Highgate - and set a scene from The Pickwick Papers at the Inn.

The poet John Keats, artists John Constable and William Blake were also known to frequent the inn.

The origins of the name are disputed - it either derives from the Spanish Ambassador to the court of James I or to early owners Francisco and Juan Porero.

Indeed Juan is said to be one of the spectres haunting his former pub after fighting a duel with his brother over a love interest and ending up buried in the garden.

The Grade II listed building once served as a tollgate and boundary marker for the Bishop of London’s land and coaches slowing down to pass through were a target for highwaymen.

The most notorious was Dick Turpin and legend links the inn to him via his father who was reputedly the landlord.

Turpin is said to have used the pub as a hideout and a lookout point to ambush wealthy travellers leaving London.

A ghostly figure seen outside the pub is said to be the restless spirit of the highwayman who was hanged in York in 1739 for horse theft, highway robbery and murder.

A mysterious "lady in white" is reported to appear in the beer garden, while some drinkers in the bar have described feeling an unseen hand tugging at their clothes.

The Spaniards Inn also played a role during the 1780 Gordon Riots, when the landlord reportedly delayed a rioting mob with free alcohol until military reinforcements arrived to protect nearby Kenwood House.

Dojo’s research placed the Spaniards Inn just behind pubs in Yorkshire, Wiltshire, and Nottingham in their ranking of the UK’s most haunted venues.

A Dojo spokesperson said: "With Halloween just weeks away, a trip to one of the UK’s most haunted pubs is the perfect way to embrace the spooky season with a pint, and potentially a spooky encounter."
